books.name: fsent_champ_long_htfesmcl4

It stacks the HTF-side FS entry (exp_htf_fs_entry=all) with max_consecutive_losses=4, which is the one setting that clears the 2022-H2 cell that the FS entry alone re-broke. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 762t / +771.87R / DD 20.02R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 43.0%, OOS 425t / +339.08R / DD 15.04R / WR 37.8%. It buys +384R of in-sample return mostly by admitting 528 new trades rather than by improving the ones it had. Registered as the high-return end of the range so the owner can see what the ceiling costs. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0285 in sample, p = 0.5311 out of sample, gap +384.44 IS and +86.63 OOS - significant in sample, NOT out of sample. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15_htffs
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - FAILS THE DRAWDOWN BUDGET, and is registered with that stated first because it is the arm that looks best on a net column and is disqualified by a single number. fsent_champ_long_htf15 with exp_htf_fs_entry='flip'. MEASURED: IS 754t / +764.85R / DD 29.76R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 42.8%, OOS 395t / +346.08R / DD 14.74R / WR 37.9%. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: in-sample drawdown 29.62R is OVER the owner's 29R ceiling, before any consideration of the return. It also re-creates a negative half-year that its own parent does not have (htf15 has 0, this has 1), so it fails the zero-negative rule twice over. The period control passes - b = +1.05 at t = +3.29 on the half-year fixed effect, better in 5 of 6 years - so the gain itself is not a period artifact; it is the risk it carries that disqualifies it. Registered because it is the highest in-sample net measured anywhere in the fsent family, +925.79R, and burying the number that beats every other one while omitting the ceiling it breaches is the failure mode this family has been guarding against all cycle. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0105 in sample, p = 0.4904 out of sample, gap +392.43R IS and +64.58R OOS. THE STRONGEST IN-SAMPLE RESULT IN THE ENTIRE FAMILY, and not significant out of sample. Stating that pair next to each other is the point: a p of 0.0105 on its own is the number a person would quote, and the 0.4904 beside it is the number that decides. It is disqualified on the drawdown ceiling before either of them is consulted, but if that ceiling were lifted it would still be an in-sample-only result.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_htffs
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the strongest arm in this family on the owner's own rule, and the first one that adds return without adding a negative half-year. ONE parameter from the shipping book: exp_htf_fs_entry='flip', so the HTF flip-bucket window opens on the swing's FS print instead of on the break, while the decisive and b2 buckets keep their breaks. That is the selective form of the arm rejected on 2026-10-09 - 'all' was rejected partly because it collapsed flip/decisive/b2 into one fs_both set and the book stopped distinguishing regimes; this keeps two of the three intact. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 751t / +756.98R / DD 22.45R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 42.3%, OOS 388t / +313.35R / DD 14.74R / WR 36.9%. That is +364.57R in sample and +60.84R out of sample on 242 more trades. THE OWNER'S RULE: drawdown 19.78R is inside the 29R budget, and the negative half-year count is UNCHANGED at 1 - this arm does not bring back the 2025-H1 cell that htf_fs='all' re-broke, which is the specific failure that sank the earlier test. PERIOD CONTROL PASSES BOTH WAYS: with a calendar-year fixed effect b = +1.34 at t = +3.24, and with the stricter half-year fixed effect b = +1.40 at t = +3.40, better in 5 of 6 years. It is also the largest gain the half-year test has ever survived in this family. CAUSALITY IS CLEAN, measured in HTF_FS_ENTRY_REJECTED.md: window_start minus its own FS print is exactly 0.0h at min, median and max in both eras, and zero entries precede their window_start - an FS-anchored window opens precisely at the print, not before it. WHAT IT COSTS: the same objection that applies to every FS-entered window applies here - 95% of the gain sits in 197 windows the book was not trading before, trades per window roughly doubles, and the drawdown goes from 13.42R to 19.78R. The return is real and survives a period control, but it is bought with breadth rather than with a better read of the existing windows, and it is bought with 46% more drawdown than the parent. Nothing is adopted: the 2021-22 era is reused old data, not a holdout. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0272 in sample, p = 0.5956 out of sample, gap +364.57R IS and +60.84R OOS - significant IN SAMPLE ONLY. The in-sample result is the strongest of its shape in this family and the out-of-sample one is not distinguishable from a reshuffle of the parent. So the honest ranking is unchanged by this arm: fsent_champ_long_mcloff remains the only book that clears in BOTH eras (0.0312 / 0.0117), and htf15_htffs' in-sample p of 0.0105 is the single lowest in-sample figure measured anywhere in the family paired with an out-of-sample figure of 0.4904. That pattern - very strong in sample, flat out of it - is exactly what the forward window exists to distinguish, and it is the reason +364R is not a recommendation.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15_tskip6
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - fsent_champ_long_htf15 with exp_trail_skip_n=6, the strongest of the two verified skip_n books and the one where the risk improvement is largest. Same mechanism as fsent_champ_long_tskip4 and the same reason it is real: exp_trail_skip_n drops the first N trailing-stop events (unified.py:1493), converting weak early trail exits into ordinary stop exits at exactly -1.000R. Purging every stop-exit trade RAISES the net rather than lowering it (+723.83 -> +958.83 at skip_n=5), which is the opposite of a right-tail bet and is the test that killed swing shape, volatile candles and mark continuation. MEASURED, on the registry net lens (equity_quality): IS 395t / +644.04R / DD 23.93R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 40.8%, OOS 216t / +336.16R / DD 14.90R / WR 36.6%. MaxConsecL 13 IS / 11 OOS on the gross curve. Against the parent: +134.60R IS and +73.73R OOS, with IS drawdown IMPROVING 21.05 -> 18.09 and, uniquely among these books, THE WORST LOSING STREAK FALLING 22 -> 13 in sample and holding at 11 out of sample. The parent's OOS streak is 11 and this book's is 11, so nothing is traded away on the owner's stated first priority. WHY 6. Chosen on risk, not on the net argmax: skip_n=32 posts +875.80R IS but its OOS is +218.70 against the parent's +254.81 - it LOSES - and its IS DD is 26.65 with an OOS DD of 27.00. The DD-safe window here is 2..6, wider than the parent's 3..6, and 6 is the best net inside it. The value ladder is genuinely still rising past the value chosen, which is the honest reason not to push further: this is the top of the safe window, not a plateau, and the next rung costs drawdown. OOS WAS READ ONCE at the IS-selected value. CAVEAT CARRIED: OOS drawdown rises 9.98 -> 12.98. The in-sample drawdown gain does not carry out of sample; the losing streak and the net do. fsent_champ_short is out of scope by owner ruling. fsent_champ_long_htffs is deliberately NOT registered: its only DD-safe value is skip_n=2 and that LOSES on OOS (+281.75 against the parent's +313.35), and its +2570R at skip_n=32 costs DD 12.86 -> 30.05 and MaxConsecL 12 -> 23.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_tskip4
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - fsent_champ_long with exp_trail_skip_n=4, and the first result in this repo whose edge was CONFIRMED BY MECHANISM rather than by a net that survived OOS. exp_trail_skip_n drops the first N trailing-stop events outright (unified.py:1493, _trail_skip_rem -= 1; _tr_ok = False). WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, and this is the part worth reading: it does NOT improve exits on the same trades, it CONVERTS trail exits into stop exits. On the parent, 497 of 497 trades exit on the trail and ZERO hit the stop; at skip_n=5 it inverts to 185 trail and 244 SL. So the knob is turning trailing stops off for the first few moves, and positions that would have closed early at a small profit instead ride until the stop. EVERY one of those converted trades exits at exactly -1.000R - median and 10th percentile identical - so they are ordinary losses, not oversized ones, and they are the same weak trades the trail was closing for scraps. THE PURGE TEST IS WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE FOUR HYPOTHESES THAT DIED BEFORE IT. At the pin there is nothing to purge, because almost nothing exits on the stop. Above skip_n=4 the stop population is large, and removing every stop-exit trade RAISES the net on all three books tested (+616 -> +860 on long, +724 -> +959 on htf15, +1505 -> +1834 on htffs). A right-tail bet loses exactly that way, because its gain lives in the trades the filter removes. Here the survivors go from -0.20 to +2.31 median R. That is selection, not variance. MEASURED, on the registry net lens (equity_quality, which is what these pins use): IS 439t / +578.96R / DD 23.77R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 41.2%, OOS 235t / +269.27R / DD 15.90R / WR 40.0%. Against the parent that is +63.50R IS and +45.21R OOS, and the IS DRAWDOWN IMPROVES, 19.57 -> 17.99. WHY 4 AND NOT 5. The value was chosen on the owner's stated priority - drawdown and losing streak first - not on the net argmax. skip_n=32 posts +974.53R on IS, nearly double, and holds on OOS at +416.23R; it is rejected because its DD is 22.24 against the parent's 19.57 and its OOS DD is 26.44 against 9.85. The DD-safe window on this book is 3,4,5,6 and 4 is the best net inside it. OOS WAS READ ONCE, at the value IS selected, which is the discipline the last three hypotheses all failed. WHAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS: OOS drawdown RISES, 9.85 -> 12.05. The IS drawdown gain does not carry out of sample; what carries is the net and the losing streak. If OOS drawdown matters equally, skip_n=3 is the only value free on both eras (+230.92R OOS at DD 10.53) and it is the smaller prize. OWNER SCOPE: fsent_champ_short was ruled out of this work by the owner on 2026-10-14 and is deliberately NOT registered - short loses at every skip_n above 2, so the knob is not a family rule. THE SHORTCUT THAT WAS CORRECTED HERE, because it is the one this repo keeps making: the first census swept skip_n in {0,1,2,3,5}, found 5 best on all three books, and that is a BOUNDARY ARTEFACT - 5 was the top of the grid. Extended to 32 the IS argmax is 32 on all three books, and htf15 at 32 LOSES on OOS. The census number was never a promotion and was not treated as one.

This one reaches +616.17R while staying honest about what a regime is. Adding the htf15 swing buys +49.59R IS and dilutes the cohort variance at the same time, so the recommendation on EVIDENCE remains mcloff and the recommendation on RETURN is this one. Still NOT adopted: no arm in the family has forward evidence, and 12 observations of a half-year table is not a guarantee. See method/RESEARCH_COMPLETE.md and method/GRID_PERIOD_AND_KNOB_GUARD.md. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0115 in sample, p = 0.1445 out of sample, gap +82.80 IS and +37.76 OOS - significant in sample, NOT out of sample - the era that matters. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the only arm found so far that fixes the shipping book's one negative half-year WITHOUT losing return, and it does so by moving a knob almost nobody has touched: the HTF swing length. THIS IS THE ONE FROM THE OWNER'S OWN RULE. Asked on 2026-10-09 for something that never goes negative - 'kabhi negative nahi hona chahiye' - the sweep of the HTF plane (1h swings, min_bars 10 -> 3..40) found that fsent_champ_long's single negative half-year, 2025-H1 at -0.7R, disappears at min_bars 13 and the net RISES from +773.0R to +796.5R (14) and +822.4R (15). MEASURED: IS 490t / +502.76R / DD 26.26R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 41.2%, OOS 274t / +256.61R / DD 10.32R / WR 37.1%. Against the parent that is +34.2R IS and +15.3R OOS on 8 and 31 fewer trades. WHY THIS IS NOT A GRID PEAK: the region around it is a genuine plateau, not a spike. min_bars 12 gives +783.5R but still 1 negative cell; 13 gives +787.6R with 0; 14 +796.5R with 0; 15 +822.4R with 0; 16 +746.1R with 0; 18 falls back to +708.7R with 1 negative again. By contrast min_bars 30 posts the single best number in the whole sweep at +847.3R with 0 negative - and is a SPIKE: 24 gives +645.4R with 2 negatives, 28 gives +659.6R with 2, 32 gives +696.3R with 0, 34 gives +562.5R. A 200R peak with a 60R trough either side is not an edge, so 30 is rejected and 15 is kept. WHAT CHANGED MECHANICALLY: the HTF plane is engine slot 2 and its swing series feeds the leg ratio, the bias-momentum breaks, the bias flips and _sw_ts_dir_mag, which is the flip/decisive classification every trade is tagged with. A longer 1h leg means fewer, larger HTF windows - 1601 swings at min_bars 10 down to 1479 at 15 - so the regime the router sees is coarser and it sits on fewer regime flips. That is why it is a genuinely different book rather than a re-tuned one. NOTE ON REGISTRATION: the HTF swing length is NOT an engine parameter, it is the registry's `swing` FIELD selecting a precomputed series, so this book needs the `htf15` series added to run_experiment.get_data - it is there, built at min_bars=15 on the 1h flow candles. A book that wanted a different HTF length would need its own series there, not a params edit. STILL NOT ADOPTED: period control gives b=+0.5681 IS and +0.3723 OOS, both positive with 97-98% of the raw gap surviving the half-year fixed effect, so it is not a regime proxy - but both cells are UNDERPOWERED against their own MDEs (1.0372 and 0.8050), so the magnitude is not established. In-sample drawdown rises 13.42R -> 17.28R and OOS 11.88R -> 16.86R, which fits the owner's 29R budget but is a real cost. And the OOS window is 2021-22, which is not a holdout - see method/OOS_IS_NOT_A_HOLDOUT.md. See method/HTF_SWEEP_OWNER_RULE.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mcloff
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - and the best-EVIDENCED one in the registry. It changes ONE INTEGER: max_consecutive_losses from 3 to 0, which turns the loss-run cutoff OFF. The autopsy of the parent's negative half-year found 2025-H1 was not a disaster but a coin flip that landed red: 60 trades, net -0.69R, mean -0.011R per trade, 20 winners making +29.6R against 40 losers making -30.3R. In that exact situation the cutoff is not protecting the book, it is cutting winners - it stops the book right before the recovery trade that follows every streak. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 524t / +502.69R / DD 23.30R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 39.7%, OOS 293t / +216.03R / DD 11.05R / WR 37.1%. Compare fsent_champ_long_htf15 (underpowered), fsent_champ_long_biasmom05 (b NEGATIVE and significant at t = -9.63 OOS) and htf_fs=all (underpowered). Still NOT adopted: the period control compares this arm to champ_long, NOT to absolute zero, and a book that is meaningfully better than its parent can still be negative in some unseen half-year. The cutoff also has a real purpose under position sizing, which is a risk decision and not a signal decision. Forward evidence does not exist for it yet. See method/MAXCONSEC_LOSSES_FINDING.md. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0312 in sample, p = 0.0117 out of sample, gap +33.22 IS and +31.32 OOS - the only book in the family significant in BOTH eras. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

MEASURED: IS 415t / +505.72R / DD 19.40R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 45.2%, OOS 224t / +201.65R / DD 7.33R / WR 46.8%. Out-of-sample drawdown 7.99R and win rate 46.8% are the best numbers on this entry anywhere in the family, and the period control is positive (b = +0.42 at t = +1.81 half-year, better in 3 of 6 years) though the weakest of the three. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: it adds a negative half-year that sig_multi does not have - sig_multi is one of only two books in this family with ZERO negative cells, and this arm gives that up. Trading the single best-behaved shape in the family for a wider one is a bad exchange at this ratio, and the owner does not trade there. Registered with that named, because the out-of-sample numbers on it are the best in the family and the reason they are not adopted is not that they are bad - it is that the rule they break is the one the book was chosen for. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.5091 in sample, p = 0.9708 out of sample, gap +132.95R IS and -5.11R OOS - NOT significant in either era, and the out-of-sample gap is NEGATIVE. Worth being blunt about the ordering here, because the risk numbers point the other way: this arm has the best out-of-sample drawdown (7.99R) and the best out-of-sample win rate (46.8%) anywhere in the family, and it is the one whose edge is least distinguishable from its parent. Good risk profile is not evidence of edge, and a book can be quietly pleasant to hold and still be indistinguishable from reshuffling its parent's trades.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_atr_low
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - blocked on drawdown against the owner's 20R budget, not on the invented 11.88R gate (withdrawn 2026-10-08 as mine, not the framework's). fsent_champ_long with mode='atr_low' - the atr_high inversion: decisive windows when 15m bars are QUIET, not big. Only the mode changes; every other knob identical. This is the strongest of the four on the framework's own buckets: it WINS bucket 1 outright in both eras - IS 599t / +517.64R[as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)]/ expectancy 1.125 / PF 3.22 against the base 528t / +533.4R / 1.010 / 3.09, and OOS 261t / +187.96R/ 0.891 / 2.96 against 311t / +239.6R / 0.770 / 2.69 - on MORE trades than the base, so more evidence and not less. Its out-of-sample tail is also the healthiest in the set (top 5% contributes 71.2% against the base's 81.1%; removing the top 10% still leaves -4.6% against -11.7%; removing the top 5% leaves 26.3% against 16.3%) and its DD expansion is 0.51, i.e. half its out-of-sample drawdown is in-sample. It is blocked purely on bucket 2 and bucket 9: 28.9R max DD in sample against the owner's 20R budget, 82 trades to make the drawdown, 460 trades underwater against the base's 286, and a 16-trade losing streak against the base's 11. Its own threshold swept 0.20-0.60 and the OOS gain peaks sharply at 0.35 (+41.1R) and is NEGATIVE everywhere else - one point, not a region, which is exactly the grid-peak failure P69 warns about. This is the one candidate worth keeping open, and the open question is whether a 20R budget can stretch to 29R - the owner's call, not the registry's. See method/OWNER_SCORECARD_MODES.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_causalfloor
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED. **The name is historical and wrong - this is NOT a causality fix, and nothing about it is a fix at all.** It is fsent_champ_long with one number changed: exp_window_floor_s, the wait between a window opening and the LTF entry being allowed, from the shipped 2700 seconds to 7200 seconds. That is the whole mechanism: a longer wait, not a corrected one. It came out of a sweep of that one parameter, 7200 was the best value found, and a value chosen by a sweep carries selection pressure - it was not derived from a rule.  IT WAS ORIGINALLY REGISTERED AS A CAUSALITY FIX AND THAT WAS WRONG. The first description claimed the shipped gate let an LTF entry run up to 900 seconds before its 1h window candle closed, and that this book removed those trades. That claim was withdrawn on 2026-10-10 - the six trades it pointed at sit exactly on the boundary, where the 15m bar closes at the same instant the 1h window closes, which is legal. method/WINDOW_FLOOR_LEAK.md, which carried the finding, was deleted with it; this text is the correction. Read method/WITHDRAWN_WINDOW_LOOKAHEAD.md before believing anything here about causality.  MEASURED against the parent (528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS, 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS): IS 513 / +529.84R / DD 13.62R / WR 39.6%, OOS 308 / +248.90R / DD 11.88R / WR 38.0%. It earns LESS in sample and about the same out of sample - it gives up trades to buy a smaller drawdown, and on this evidence it does not buy enough.  The book does have ZERO negative half-years where the parent has one, but that is NOT a regime discovery and must not be read as one: across 155 half-year cells the 6 negative ones are indistinguishable from the 149 positive ones in loss concentration (35.2% vs 36.1%) and losing-streak length (8.3 vs 8.1). The same expectancy is landing slightly red, not a condition that can be filtered. That finding lives in method/PERIOD_2025H1_WHAT_HAPPENED.md.  FOR THE RECORD, since it bounds every causality claim in this family: a slack audit on 2026-10-10 (exp_window_slack_audit.py, 29 books, both eras, 22154 trades) measured the gap between each trade's decision instant and the close of its 1h window candle. The gate at unified.py:1034 is permissive by 900 seconds in principle, but ZERO trades anywhere in the family landed in that band - the distribution is 21992 trades at 900s or more of clearance, 147 exactly on the boundary, and none between. The shipping book is clean at 311 of 311. The 15 apparent violations are all fsent_champ_long_mode_union and are a REPORTING defect in that book's window_start field, not lookahead - see method/WINDOW_SLACK_AUDIT.md.  PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.7256 in sample, p = 0.0230 out of sample, gap -3.52 IS / +9.31 OOS - out of sample only, and negative in sample. Significance here means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's. It does NOT mean the book is better in absolute terms; the same audit shows it is not. See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_sig_multi_acc
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - and the name is the point. This book was found BY ACCIDENT while testing a lean max_positions=1 serial base: the owner asked for a base with very few filters to test hypotheses on, ten knobs were censused, and exp_mltf=1 was the only one that improved both eras. It was registered under the serial framing until the concurrency was checked, at which point it was found to run UP TO 7 SIMULTANEOUS POSITIONS. It is a multi book and the _acc suffix keeps that provenance visible so nobody later reads it as a serial finding. NOT A DISCOVERY: unified.py:41 already documents exp_mltf as the entire multi edge ('With the gate on, the same config is +137.72R IS but -13.26R OOS over 230 trades. Turning it off gives +325.78R IS / +70.15R OOS'). What was added here is a confirmation that it also works on a thin base, and the note below that the sweep almost produced a false serial result. max_positions IS INERT WHEN exp_mltf IS ON - measured byte-identical, same trade-set sha ad4399fcf1 IS and bc92bc0329 OOS at max_positions 1 and at 0, with 7 concurrent in sample and 5 out of sample at BOTH settings. So the value is written as 0 to match observed behaviour rather than 1 to match the base it was derived from. That is the same class of finding as chop_thresh being inert under mode=atr_high: a config key that states an intention the code does not carry out. THIN BASE - it is fsent_sig_sw10_short with exp_mltf and NOTHING else, so it lacks all five filters its siblings carry (exp_bias_momentum_min 0.8, exp_fs_small_swing 6.0, exp_skip_weekend 1, exp_trail_skip_n 2, and htffs also exp_htf_fs_entry flip). MEASURED on the registry net lens: IS 472t / +441.93R / DD 12.67R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 41.3%, OOS 301t / +226.33R / DD 12.17R / WR 40.7%. AGAINST ITS SIBLINGS, NOT A CLEAN WIN, and the awkward parts are recorded rather than buried. vs fsent_sig_multi: better in both nets (+75.41R IS, +38.14R OOS) and better IS drawdown (12.67 against 13.43), but WORSE out-of-sample drawdown by 4.57R (12.18 against 7.61) and a lower net win rate (0.386 against 0.445). vs fsent_sig_multi_htffs: better out of sample (+23.18R) but 63.15R WORSE in sample. Ranked across the 42 exp_mltf multi books: IS net 21st, OOS net 11th, IS drawdown 3rd of 42 - the best in-sample drawdown in that set - and OOS drawdown 11th. THE ONE THING IT IS BEST AT: it is the only arm in the entire ten-knob census that REPAIRS a negative half-year instead of adding one - 2022-H2 goes -2.94R to +16.94R out of sample - and it posts zero negative half-years in both eras (8 of 8 IS, 4 of 4 OOS) while its own parent posts one. TAIL DEPENDENCE IS BETTER THAN THE PARENT'S, which is the opposite of every other candidate in this series: removing the ten largest out-of-sample trades leaves the parent at 9.39R, 8% of itself, and this at 104.22R, 47% of the ratio. THE ONE AXIS THAT WORSENS: in-sample max losing streak 9 to 12, out-of-sample unchanged at 11. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: the serial gate it was supposed to be is inoperative, the family already has two multi books with more filters on it, and its case rests on breadth that the siblings already have. Registered because the thin-base confirmation is a real measurement and because the sweep that produced it is worth keeping.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_chop
books.desc: REGISTERED FOR COMPLETENESS, NOT A CANDIDATE - and the interesting thing about it is how close it is to doing nothing. mode='chop' instead of mode='atr_high': the regime classifier that decides whether a bar belongs to the decisive or the flip bucket now reads a chop threshold (chop_thresh=58.0) instead of an ATR percentile band. EVERY ONE of the other 31 fsent books is mode='atr_high', so this axis had never been registered anywhere in the family and the 2026-10-09 HTF-FS rejection only ever spoke to the ATR classifier. MEASURED in sample it is the shipping book exactly: 528 / +533.37 / DD 13.42, identical n, net and drawdown to fsent_champ_long. Out of sample it diverges slightly - 294 / +244.45 / DD 11.88 against the parent's 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 - so the two classifiers agree on every bar of the in-sample era and part company on 17 trades out of sample. CONCLUSION WORTH KEEPING: the regime classifier is NOT a live axis on this book. Swapping ATR for chop moves the number by less than half a percent of the net, and in sample not at all, so no result in this family should be attributed to the classifier rather than to the things that actually move it. Registered because an axis that was never measured should not stay that way, and because 'we never tested the chop classifier' is exactly the sentence that let the 2026-09 HTF-FS test be read as a general result. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 1.0000 in sample, p = 0.7603 out of sample, gap +0.00R IS and +4.86R OOS. p = 1.0000 is not a rounding curiosity and is worth reading carefully: the in-sample trade list is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the shipping book's, so the permutation is comparing the parent against itself and 1.0000 is the correct answer rather than a null result. It is the precise form of the claim above - the chop classifier and the ATR classifier select the same bars on every in-sample bar, so this is not a small effect, it is no effect at all on half the data.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_flip_quality
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - DISQUALIFIED 2026-10-08 as a regime proxy. fsent_champ_long with mode='flip_quality' - B2/flip by chop AND a HTF-magnitude floor, so it filters the chop branch. It held the base drawdown exactly (13.4R IS / 11.9R OOS) and was ahead on all three books of its family in the lane test (+4.8R / +4.8R / +54.0R), which is why it was the closest of the four. Period control then disqualified it: the mode is IN-SAMPLE INERT on all three books. In IS the arm and the base take the SAME trades - 0 new, 0 dropped on fsent_utcsat_long and fsent_champ_short, and on this book the entire +1.41R is ONE dropped trade - so all three IS cells are non-estimable and every R of the mode's effect is out of sample. Out of sample b after a half-year fixed effect is +0.2122 against an MDE of 0.8569: inside the noise floor, 96% of the raw gap explained by the calendar. The one powered cell is fsent_champ_short OOS (b +1.3963, t 2.016) - the FS-short mirror, a different architecture with 23.9R drawdown, and the source of the whole +54.01R - and one cell of one architecture on one era cannot carry the other five. The earlier 3-of-3 lane result was real and was not sufficient; being drawdown-neutral is not the same as being useful. Two corrections recorded on 2026-10-08: the 'fails on both second lanes (-7.0R, -4.1R)' sentence was measured on champion_multi_sw10/utcsat_multi_sw10, a DIFFERENT architecture (pivot_rule=origin, no FS side, no exp_mltf), and the first period-control harness labelled survivors as cohort=1, which produced a meaningless t of 7.672. Remains registered and pinned so the measurements are re-derivable. The branch also READS chop_thresh, which is not in this book's config, so it was never the base plus a mode string. See method/FLIP_QUALITY_PERIOD_CONTROL.md, method/MODE_CONFIRM2_RIGHT_LANES.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_fd
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED. fsent_champ_long with mode='fd' - fractional-dimension regime: low FD=trend->flip, high FD=range->B2. Closest drawdown of the four (13.4R IS / 12.2R OOS) but still worse than base, and fails out of sample on both second lanes.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_biasmom05
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the HTF-side sibling of fsent_champ_long_htf15, and the one that fixes the negative half-year WITHOUT adding drawdown. Where htf15 lengthens the 1h leg, this arms the other HTF knob: exp_bias_momentum_min=0.5, a floor on the RATIO of this HTF leg's magnitude to the previous one, so the book only takes entries while the 1h leg is growing rather than shrinking. It is the closest existing knob to 'the HTF window opens on strength' - it is literally the 1h leg's own measure deciding whether its window counts. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 456t / +459.33R / DD 22.78R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 39.5%, OOS 251t / +182.78R / DD 7.87R / WR 37.6%. THE POINT OF THIS BOOK IS ITS DRAWDOWN: in-sample max DD is 13.42R, EXACTLY the parent's, and out-of-sample is 13.47R against the parent's 11.88R - a 1.6R cost. Every other arm that removes the negative half-year pays for it in drawdown; this one does not. It costs return instead: -31.9R IS and -22.5R OOS, on 40 and 24 fewer trades. It is the low-drawdown branch of the owner's rule, against htf15's high-return branch (IS DD 17.28R, OOS 16.86R, but IS +567.57R / OOS +254.88R). Both are registered so the choice is visible rather than averaged. ZERO negative half-years out of 12, same as htf15. NOTE: this knob is ON the sig books at 0.8 and OFF on the champ books, and 0.8 was chosen there - see fsent_sig_multi. It was never swept on the champ architecture, which is why 0.5 and 1.0 were only measured here for the first time. Still NOT adopted: no period control has been run on this arm, the negative-cell removal has not been shown to survive a half-year fixed effect, and the OOS window is 2021-22, which is not a holdout - see method/OOS_IS_NOT_A_HOLDOUT.md. See method/HTF_SWEEP_OWNER_RULE.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_trailhalf
books.desc: CANDIDATE: fsent_champ_long + exp_trail_half=1. Multi check on 2026-10-06: OOS +287.0 / avgR 1.032 / PF 3.00 / DD 16.5 vs base +245.0 / 0.793 / 2.76 / 11.9. Lifts total and per-trade, at DD cost. NOT adopted - needs exp_port_differential parity + cohort autopsy first.

books.name: fsent_sig_multi
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the strongest non-shipping result in the repo, and still not an adoption. fsent_sig_full's entire filter set (bias_momentum 0.8, fs_small_swing 6.0, trail_skip_n 2, weekends skipped, FS entry on shorts, ext_stop_r 3.0, halt on 3) with max_positions 1 -> 0, i.e. the single-slot gate removed and concurrency enabled. ONE value differs from fsent_sig_full; the other 15 are identical. WHAT IT IS, in plain terms: the same signals, and the book simply stops standing aside. Of 50 extra out-of-sample trades, 48 were taken while a serial position was already open and only 2 after it closed; 47 of the 50 joined a position in the SAME direction, so this is adding to an existing bet rather than hedging. Those extras earned +25.1R at a 46% win rate, against -0.3R given up on trades the serial book took instead. In sample the same mechanism gives 108 extras earning +186.2R for a net +188.8R. MEASURED: IS 291t / +366.04R / DD 13.43R [as of 2026-10-15 (exp_repin_all.py, net lens)] / WR 45.6%, OOS 185t / +184.86R / DD 5.81R / WR 47.2%. Against the shipping book out of sample that is 92% of the net on 63% of the trades, at 64% of the drawdown, with a 10-point better win rate, and BOTH direction columns stay alive (+136.7R long, +83.1R short) which matters because the FS-side autopsy found the two families pointing in opposite directions. GATES: period control positive in both eras with 99% of the raw gap surviving, so this is NOT a regime proxy - the ATR% ceiling's signature does not appear. The half-year partition is 12 of 12. Tail dependence IMPROVES in every cell of both eras: removing the top 10 trades leaves 40.1% of in-sample profit against the parent's 22.0%, and 30.7% out of sample against 22.4%, which is the opposite of mode_union's 96%. WHY IT IS NOT ADOPTED - CORRECTED 2026-10-08, because the original reason was wrong. I previously wrote here that the out-of-sample magnitude is underpowered (b +0.3303 against an MDE of 2.1999) and therefore should not be adopted. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN. The 'OOS' era is 2021-01-01 to 2022-12-31 and IS is 2023-01-01 to 2026-09-13 - the OOS window is two years OLDER than the in-sample window and has been re-scored many times. It is not a holdout and never was, as method/FORWARD_TEST_PLAN.md states in its own second paragraph ('reused many times, not a holdout'). A power gate on that window is a real measurement of a real limitation OF THAT WINDOW and is not a forward verdict in either direction: it does not say this arm is bad, it says we have no forward data on it. THE CORRECT REASON THIS IS NOT ADOPTED: the adoption decision is BLOCKED ON FORWARD DATA, which does not exist on this machine. method/FORWARD_TEST_PLAN.md is ACTIVE with a hard boundary at 2026-09-13 10:03 IST and five pre-registered gates; it was scored once on 2026-09-25 and produced 5 trades and NO VERDICT (n<50); data/forward/bybit/ is not present locally now. This book is NOT on the contract's pre-registered candidate list, and because no forward window exists on disk nothing is burned - so it can be added before a new window starts, which is the cheapest high-value action available. The in-sample magnitude IS powered (b +2.1619, t +2.240, MDE 1.8920, month-cluster bootstrap +1.8501) and the 2021-22 magnitude is not (b +0.3303, MDE 2.1999); both are true and neither is a forward statement. The 2.16-vs-0.33 gap is a 2023-26 versus 2021-22 difference and should have been labelled as such when first reported. The tightest partition cells matter: 2021-H1 is +39.6 against +39.9 and 2021-H2 +35.8 against +40.5, so the FIRST out-of-sample half-year is worth almost nothing and the gain is concentrated in 2022-H1 and 2022-H2. DO NOT carry the in-sample +2.16R per trade as a forward expectation; the honest figure is roughly +0.33R and even that is not established. Concurrency shape: depth 5 in sample, 4 out, but 69% of entries happen with nothing else open, so this is the same book that occasionally takes a second position, not a crowded one. A cap of 3 costs 1.5R in sample, nothing out of sample, and lowers drawdown in both eras - a free bound on the tail. Two notes on measurement, both of which cost real time and are recorded so they are not repeated: the sibling sweep on the multi books returns BYTE-IDENTICAL results because those books carry exp_mltf=True, which bypasses the max_positions gate entirely in the harness - so this knob is inert on them and meaningful only on the serial sig book; and max_positions must be set alongside the regime knobs rather than alone, since a 0.40% min-stop floor on this book costs 4.1% of the long book's net in sample against 4.1% gained out of sample. See method/SIG_MULTI_STUDY.md.

verdict.headline: NO BOOK IS CLEARED FOR DEPLOYMENT
verdict.reason: Thirteen book variants were explored. The multiple-testing correction was not applied when the shortlist was made, and when it was applied it failed: PBO 0.57-1.00 against a 0.15 bar, and Deflated Sharpe fails for all thirteen books in both eras. The history does not identify which variant to trade.
verdict.closest_note: 107 and 108 each fail exactly one criterion out of eighteen, both in survivability. 106 and 109 overlap 85-93% with them, so choosing between the four is closer to picking three than four.
verdict.next_step: Forward evidence on a frozen candidate, scored once. The standard operational gate is 20-50 round trips or one quarter; the forward window currently holds about one month.
